title: Suggestions: risk badge visual exploration (color, iconography, a11y)
creator: Tessa Morgan
description:
Goal: explore visual treatments for the “Risk” indicator on the Optimization Suggestions (beta) list + details drawer. Risk is explicitly performance/reliability risk (not security/privacy). Exploration should land on a badge style that is readable at table density, accessible (contrast, color-blind safe), and does not over-index on alarming red/green semantics.

Context
- Risk label shows Low / Medium / High on each suggestion row and in details drawer summary.
- Users: platform engineers + ML engineers scanning a dense table; risk badge needs to be parseable in <1s.
- Must work in light + dark theme, and when printed/screenshot in grayscale.
- Must not be confused with “Security risk.” (We will solve mostly with copy/tooltip, but visual should avoid shield/lock motifs.)

Where badge appears
1) Suggestions table column: “Risk” (primary surface)
2) Suggestion details drawer header: summary row (secondary)
3) Tooltips: hover/focus on badge and/or info icon to show explanation + ‘What changes might happen’ guardrails.

Constraints / non-goals
- No new semantic color tokens without design systems sign-off; prefer using existing status tokens if possible.
- Do not rely on color alone to communicate severity.
- Keep the badge width predictable to avoid table jitter.

Exploration directions
A) Pill badge (solid fill) + text only
- Low: green fill, Medium: amber fill, High: red fill
- Pros: highly scannable
- Cons: strong red/green semantics; can read like “good/bad” rather than “risk”; high attention draw in a dense table; solid fills can fail contrast in dark theme unless carefully tuned.

B) Pill badge (subtle tint) + text + icon
- Low: subtle green tint + “Low” + circle-check
- Medium: subtle amber tint + “Medium” + triangle-exclamation
- High: subtle red tint + “High” + octagon-exclamation
- Pros: icon helps non-color differentiation; subtle tint reduces alarm
- Cons: check icon risks implying “safe/approved”; octagon (stop sign shape) can be too loud and reads like an error state.

C) Neutral pill + colored left border (or dot) + text
- Badge background stays neutral; severity indicated by a 2px left border and/or dot; text always “Low/Medium/High”
- Pros: minimal visual noise; consistent contrast; works in grayscale better than full fill; less likely to trigger “error” alarm
- Cons: dot/border alone can be missed at a glance; needs sufficient size and spacing.

D) Outlined chip + severity glyph (shape-coded) + text
- Outline color varies; inside uses glyph shape (●, ▲, ■) + label
- Pros: strongest non-color encoding; very printable; smallest space footprint
- Cons: can look “systemy”/non-native; glyph semantics require learning.

Recommendation (v1 for beta)
- Use option C as base: neutral pill with severity text + small leading dot.
- Dot color differentiates severity; text always present.
- Avoid shield/lock iconography. Avoid checkmark.
- Keep badge widths fixed by using “Med” vs “Medium” in the table only (details drawer can use full “Medium”).

Proposed spec (table)
- Content: “Low” | “Med” | “High” (shorten only in table to reduce width; tooltip shows full)
- Layout: [colored dot] [label]
- Background: neutral surface (same across levels)
- Border: neutral stroke (same across levels) OR no border if background sufficiently distinct from table cell.
- Dot color tokens (tentative):
  - Low: success-600 (but do not use full success green fill)
  - Medium: warning-600
  - High: danger-600
- If design system pushes back on danger color semantics, alternate palette: Low=blue, Medium=amber, High=purple + copy carries meaning. (We should only do this if “red” is interpreted as outage/error by users in critique.)

Proposed spec (details drawer)
- Use full words: “Low / Medium / High” + “Performance risk” label nearby (copy) to prevent security confusion.
- Drawer has more space; we can include a small info icon with tooltip.

Accessibility notes (to validate in implementation)
- Contrast: label text must meet WCAG AA (4.5:1) against badge background. If background is neutral and label text is standard text color, we are good; dot is decorative but should be visible.
- Do not encode severity with color alone: label text always present.
- Keyboard/focus: tooltip must be reachable via tab (badge treated like a button or include adjacent info icon).
- Color vision deficiency: dot colors are helpful but not sufficient; “Low/Med/High” text is primary.
- Screen readers: announce as “Risk: Low (performance/reliability).” Tooltip content should be available as accessible description on focus.

Open questions
- Abbreviation: “Med” in table acceptable? (More compact and consistent width; check with PM/UX research.)
- Do we need a “Unknown”/“Not enough data” badge variant? (Design is mostly handled by empty states, but row-level unknown could show up with partial telemetry.)

Links
- Design spec: suggestions risk definitions + copy: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/risk-level-definition-and-copy-guidelines.json
- Related design tickets: DES-640 (final badge + tooltip copy), DES-669 (a11y review)

Deliverable
- Final recommendation + a small set of tokenized styles to hand to Nora (frontend) and align with Design Systems.
comments: 2026-02-07 (Kenji Nakamura): Started with solid-fill pills but it’s reading too much like status/error. Moving toward neutral chip + dot + text. Will bring 3 variants to critique: (1) solid fill, (2) tinted fill, (3) neutral + dot.

2026-02-10 (Tessa Morgan, design critique): +1 neutral base. Avoid red fill blocks in dense table; it competes with Savings column and makes page feel “on fire”. Also avoid shield/lock icons—risk is not security.
2026-02-11 (Alicia Perez): Tested quick grayscale screenshot: solid fills collapse; neutral chip with dot + label holds up best. Suggest fixed-width chip to avoid column jitter when sorting.
2026-02-12 (George Mbatha): From prior studies, users over-interpret checkmarks as “recommended/safe”. Avoid check icon for Low risk. Text label is enough; keep tooltip strong.

2026-02-14 (Kenji Nakamura): Proposed table labels: Low / Med / High. Drawer uses Low / Medium / High and includes “Performance risk” microcopy. Next: align colors with DS tokens and verify dark mode contrast.

2026-02-18 (Tessa Morgan): Decision for beta: neutral chip + dot + text. Colors use existing warning/danger tokens but only for dot (not background). Follow-up: DES-640 for tooltip copy + microcopy to disambiguate from security risk.

2026-02-24 (Kenji Nakamura): Marking done. Handed spec to ENG via Figma notes and linked to DES-640/DES-669. Implementation note: ensure tooltip is focusable and announced by SR (aria-describedby) and do not rely on hover-only.
